text:
sam: Heads up — noticed a ~30% drop in tokens/sec for production continuous-batching after yesterday's merge (PR #4321). Paging the runtime crew.

nina: saw it in the dashboards too, latency p95 up and queueing time increased. Repro in staging with the same load pattern.

raj: interesting — my initial profiler points at scheduler changes in 7f3a1c4 (the adaptive-window heuristic). Kernel selection looks fine.

emily: can you paste the perf CI failure?

ci-bot: perf-check: continuous-batching tokens/sec baseline=12.4k tokens/s, new=8.7k tokens/s ( -29.8% ), test=quantized-llama-13b, env=staging.

sam: marking rollback candidate. @li can you bisect? start at merge commit of PR #4321 -> head of main.

li: running bisect now, will report back. quick note: cache hit rate looked lower on hosts 4/10 in Grafana (KV cache miss spike). Could be related to batching alignment?

infra-bot: deploy event: deploy main @ 1760995600 by ci-bot (includes PR #4321).

raj: KV cache miss spike + longer queueing smells like batching boundary changes — requests getting split across batches and losing prefix reuse. The scheduler change shifted batch cut thresholds.

nina: I captured a short trace from staging:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] request A arrives: seq_len 512
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] request B arrives: seq_len 8
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] scheduler batches: A alone (cut by max_seq heuristic), B waits 60ms to fill batch -> cache not reused
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] runtime: kernel selection chooses matmul-kernel-v2 for A
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] KV cache: miss for B (old cache shard), hit for A
```

li: bisect update: culprit narrowed to commit 7f3a1c4 -> 9b1e2f0, specifically cfe2d9a toggled the batching-window fallback. Reproduces locally with the perf harness.

emily: is there an easy revert? PR 4321 had a couple of unrelated tidy-ups + the scheduler patch. We can revert only the scheduler patch if we have a clean revert commit.

sam: revert candidate: revert commit cfe2d9a (temporary) and run perf CI. If that restores tokens/sec we plan a hotfix revert to main.

raj: I also ran profiler (flame graphs) — the new scheduler increases time spent in queueing and memcpy around KV shards. Sample: queue_wait median 48ms -> 93ms; memcpy 1.2ms -> 3.9ms.

nina: also noticed more heterogeneous batch sizes: more small batches (~<4) which hurts GPU utilization. Batch size median dropped 12 -> 7.

ci-bot: perf-check queued for revert-cfe2d9a: running on staging...

li: quick experiment: force old-window heuristic in runtime config -> tokens/sec back to ~12k locally. So behavior is tied to heuristic switch.

sam: ok let's proceed: create emergency revert PR for just the scheduler heuristic toggle. @emily can you own the revert and hotfix?

emily: on it. drafting revert PR now, will include perf CI run and notes about KV cache implications.

li: one more data point: kernel selection path appears slightly different due to batch shape changes — some sequences now trigger a fallback kernel that is 15% slower for short sequences. So it's multi-factor: scheduling -> batch shapes -> kernel selection + cache alignment.

raj: agreed. post-revert we should: 1) add a regression test in perf CI that does a realistic continuous-batch trace (mixed seq lengths) 2) add a telemetry gauge for batch-size histogram 3) add a KV cache shard-affinity log when cache-miss spikes occur.

nina: adding those to runtime backlog and will assign tickets. Also propose a canary rollout step for future scheduler changes (5% traffic for 24h).

infra-bot: perf CI result: revert-cfe2d9a build #2874 passed: tokens/sec restored to 12.1k tokens/s.

sam: great — merging hotfix revert. Follow-up: schedule postmortem thread with root cause analysis and long-term fixes.

emily: merged revert PR #4338 (cherry-pick revert of cfe2d9a). Rolling to prod with canary.

li: after revert, KV cache hit rates normalized and median batch size back to 11 in canary traffic.

raj: for the postmortem I'll attach flame graphs, bisect log, and the minimal reproducer harness. Also include a patch suggestion: keep the adaptive-window but add a cache-affinity-aware tie-breaker and min-batch-size gating.

nina: thanks all for quick triage. Lesson: small heuristic changes can cascade through batching -> cache -> kernel paths.

sam: filing the incident/pmo with links to perf CI, bisect notes, and the revert. Will ping the eng-sre channel to coordinate monitoring for the next 48h. :thumbsup: 

ci-bot: alert: monitor-rule "continuous-batching-tokens-per-sec" re-armed for 48h.

li: saving bisect output and harness to shared drive: //redwood/shared/perf/bisect/1761001234-cfe2d9a.txt

emily: will follow up with a short writeup in docs/runtime/notes about safer rollout practices for scheduler heuristics.

sam: closing this thread here, followups in the postmortem doc. Thanks everyone.
